title: EP 27 — A SUBAGENT IN ONE COMMAND
sub: /agents is the wizard; --agents is the headless twin
lines: A subagent is a helper with its own context, tools, and prompt.
A subagent is a helper Clawd spawns, with its own context, its own tools, and its own prompt.
The easy way to build one: run /agents — a guided wizard.
The easy way to build one is to run, slash agents. It opens a guided wizard.
Library tab, Generate with Claude, pick tools, model, save.
In the Library tab you hit Generate with Clawd, pick its tools and model, and save.
Want it scriptable? --agents takes the same fields as JSON.
Want it scriptable instead? The dash dash agents flag takes the very same fields, as JSON.
name, description, tools, model, and the system prompt.
A name, a description, the tools it may use, a model, and its system prompt.
Then just ask — and Claude delegates to the subagent.
Then you just ask. And Clawd delegates the task, straight to it.
Follow for a fresh Claude Code tip every day.
Follow for a fresh Clawd Code tip, every day.
command: claude --agents '{"slugify-explainer":{"description":"Read-only agent that explains code","prompt":"In one sentence only, say what the file does. No lists, no bug analysis, no offers to fix. Read-only; never edit files.","tools":["Read","Grep","Glob"],"model":"sonnet"}}' -p "Use the slugify-explainer agent: in one sentence, what does slugify.py do?"
